summary: The 30% order-submit failure rate is best explained by an outage/degradation of the external exchange partner behind exchange-gateway (H1, confidence 0.60, medium), not by the order-service v2.15.2 release. The failure signal originates upstream at exchange-gateway (first upstream connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example at 11:01:25Z, before order-service's first 504 at 11:02:45Z), the error signature is dominated by "exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)", and order-service's latency (~5300ms) matches the 5000ms exchange upstream timeout with flat CPU and db_pool. The deploy's timing (10:48Z, ~13 min before onset) and blast radius (exchange-gateway is not shared and not part of the changed code path) both mismatch, and the error rate stayed ~30-32% after the 11:16Z rollback. Residual uncertainty remains because the failing hop (exchange-api) has no telemetry and the rollback's execution could not be independently confirmed. Mitigation should be exchange-side (fail-fast/breaker/retry policy, partner engagement); the rollback is not expected to fix the symptom.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner (exchange-api) outage propagating to order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange partner's API (api.exchange-partner.example) began failing/degrading around 11:01Z, causing exchange-gateway connect timeouts and upstream 503s, which surfaced as 504s on the exchange-dependent subset of order-service's order-submit calls. order-service v2.15.2 is a coincidence in timing and was unrelated.

causal_chain.claim: External exchange-api at api.exchange-partner.example begins failing (connect timeouts / 503s) around 11:01Z

exchange-gateway's error_rate jumps in the 10:58 bucket to ~25% and sustains ~44% from 11:05; first upstream connect timeout at 11:01:25Z, upstream 503s from exchange-api from 11:02:20Z, circuit breaker opens at 11:03:26Z (failure ratio 0.47)
order-service calls exchange-gateway for the exchange-dependent subset of placeOrder calls and times out at the 5000ms upstream timeout, producing 504s
order-service error_rate jumps to ~30% in the 11:00 bucket (onset 10:55-11:05), latency_p99 rises to ~3264ms then ~5300ms matching the 5s exchange timeout, while CPU and db_pool_in_use stay flat
order-service 504s persist through 12:55 despite the 11:16Z rollback of dep-5333, because the fault is external

assumptions: The external partner genuinely had an incident at ~11:01Z (has_telemetry:false, so unobservable in-platform)
order-service's error set is dominated by the exchange-dependent subset, so its ~30% vs gateway's ~44% gap is fully explained
The rollback at 11:16Z was actually executed and error rate stayed flat through 12:55 as F8/F10/F11 show

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 'idempotency keys' defect causing order submit 504s (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v2.15.2 change to the order-submit handler introduced a defect (e.g. retry/duplicate-submission behaviour or a blocking call) that caused 504s on order submit; the exchange-gateway errors are a downstream symptom or unrelated noise.

causal_chain.claim: v2.15.2 'Add idempotency keys to order submit' (dep-5333) deployed 10:48Z changes the submit handler
The changed code path produces slow/failing submit requests that time out as 504s
order-service error_rate jumps to ~30% and latency_p99 to ~5300ms

assumptions: The changed handler has a defect that manifests only under live traffic ~13 minutes after deploy (warm-up, backfill, or first-triggered path)
The dominant error 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout' is a secondary effect of the local defect rather than the true origin
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing mismatch: deploy at 10:48Z but error_rate stayed flat ~0.16-0.23% through 10:55 and onset was between 10:55 and 11:05 (first order-service 504 at 11:02:45Z, first failure signal upstream at exchange-gateway 11:01:25Z) — the failure signal originates at exchange-gateway, which is NOT shared and is not part of the changed code path (F15, F16, F10, F11). The single dominant error is a 504 on exchange-gateway, and order-service CPU/db_pool stayed flat (no local resource symptom, F12), while latency matches the 5s exchange timeout. Also, the failure persisted after the 11:16Z rollback (F2, F8).

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway's own resource saturation / capacity limit causing upstream timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: exchange-gateway itself (not the external partner) exhausted a local resource (connections, threads, CPU) so its calls to the external partner timed out; the connect timeouts are a symptom of gateway-local saturation.

causal_chain.claim: exchange-gateway hits an internal resource/connection limit around 11:01Z
Outbound calls to api.exchange-partner.example time out at connect stage

assumptions: exchange-gateway has a saturation mode that shows as 'upstream connect timeout' rather than a local capacity error
No gateway config/limit change occurred (none was found in the window, F3/F4)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The error text is explicitly 'upstream connect timeout ... host=api.exchange-partner.example' plus 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' and a circuit breaker on exchange-api — a signature of the peer failing, not of gateway-local saturation (F10). exchange-gateway is not shared and received no config/deploy change in the window (F3, F4, F16). The gateway's own resource metrics were never queried (gap), but the mechanism evidence points at the external peer.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4 config change (cfg-2290) degrading the quote branch
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2290 (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4) reduced quote cache lifetime, causing more upstream market-data calls, latency/error propagation through pricing-engine into order-service's quote-dependent submit path.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2290 reduces pricing-engine cache TTL 5→4 at 09:20Z
Shorter TTL increases market-data-service / redis-cache load and pricing-engine latency
order-service submit path calling pricing-engine slows and times out

assumptions: A 1-second TTL reduction is enough to cause failures
The 100-minute gap between the change and onset is a delayed effect rather than a coincidence
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-2290 is on a different branch of the graph (order-service → pricing-engine → market-data/redis) than the failing hop (order-service → exchange-gateway → exchange-api) and occurred >1h41m before onset (F18, F3). The observed error signature names exchange-gateway, not pricing-engine, and order-service latency matches the 5s exchange timeout (F9, F10, F12).

facts.statement: Across all services in 2026-03-17T06:00Z-13:00Z there was exactly one deployment: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333), deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z, summary 'Add idempotency keys to order submit', status 'rolled_back' at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z.
The only config change in the window was cfg-2290: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5 -> 4 at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z; no feature-flag, infra/network or dependency-version change appears.

order-service error_rate was flat ~0.16-0.23% through the 10:55 bucket, then jumped to avg 19.02% (max 31.9) in the 11:00 bucket and stayed ~30-32% through 12:55, placing true onset between 10:55 and 11:05.
order-service logged 349 ERROR entries from 11:02:45Z to 12:58:54Z with a single dominant pattern: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' (first occurrence 11:02:45Z).

exchange-gateway is the origin of the failure signal: first upstream connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example at 11:01:25Z (before order-service's first 504 at 11:02:45Z), exchange-api 503s from 11:02:20Z, and a circuit breaker opening for exchange-api at 11:03:26Z (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s).

exchange-gateway error_rate jumped from ~0.17-0.23% (through 10:51) to 24.93% in the 10:58 bucket and ~43-45% sustained from 11:05, exceeding order-service's ~30%, consistent with order-service failing only the exchange-dependent subset of calls.

order-service latency_p99 jumped from ~149ms baseline to 3264.85ms in the 11:00 bucket and ~5300ms sustained from 11:05, consistent with the 5000ms exchange-gateway upstream timeout; order-service CPU (~38-41%) and db_pool_in_use (~13.6-14.5) stayed flat across onset.

order-service's dependency graph runs order-service -> exchange-gateway -> exchange-api (external, has_telemetry:false); exchange-gateway is shared:false, and exchange-api has no telemetry of its own, so the failing hop is not observable in-platform.

BLAST RADIUS MISMATCH: the failure signal originates at exchange-gateway -> external exchange-api, and the gateway is not shared with other services and is not part of the changed code path; the deployed change only altered the order-service submit handler.

cfg-2290 sits on a different branch of order-service's graph (order-service -> pricing-engine -> market-data-service/redis-cache), >1h41m before onset, and no config change exists on order-service itself.
payment-service error_rate stayed flat ~0.17-0.26% across the entire 10:30-12:57 window with no onset at 11:00, so the blast radius in error rate does not include payment-service.

Historical precedent HIST-103 (2025-10-21) 'Order failures during exchange partner outage' shares the current signature (order-service + exchange-gateway, '504 on order submit', 'upstream timeouts', root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', category dependency_failure); HIST-115 (order-service 'pool exhausted', config_change) and HIST-111 (bad_deployment) are the rollback-blind precedents.
A second deployment query restricted to the post-rollback window 11:10-13:00Z returned 0 deployments.

assumptions: The external exchange partner genuinely had an outage/degradation beginning ~11:01Z; this is unobservable in-platform (exchange-api has_telemetry:false), so it is assumed rather than verified.
order-service's error set is dominated by the exchange-dependent subset of order-submit calls, which explains the gap between order-service's ~30% and exchange-gateway's ~44% error rate.
The 11:16Z rollback was actually executed; only the 'rolled_back' status and rolled_back_at field are available, with no rollback deploy record, revert commit/PR, or rollback event id.
The error-rate series through 12:55 (~30-32%) reliably reflects the post-rollback period, since no independent order-service error_rate query was run specifically for 11:16-13:00Z.
The 'single top error pattern is a 504 on exchange-gateway' log characterization reflects the aggregate error set and not a single-sampled error line.
The absence of a config/network/dependency-version change is inferred from the change-scoped queries performed, not from a full audit of all change types.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT rely on the dep-5333 rollback as the mitigation: the error rate held ~30-32% well after the 11:16Z rollback. Treat the rollback as complete and keep order-service on the pre-v2.15.2 revision rather than roll-forward, then mitigate at the exchange hop instead.
recommended_actions.rationale: The rollback (~11:16Z) did not change the symptom: error_rate stayed ~30-32% through 12:55, and timing/blast-radius evidence places the origin upstream of the changed code path.

recommended_actions.action: Fail fast on the exchange-dependent path: at exchange-gateway, set/verify the exchange-api circuit breaker to open on error (currently opened late at 11:03:26Z, ~2 min after the first connect timeout) and shorten the connect timeout so order-submit returns a fast, well-formed error instead of hanging to the 5000ms upstream timeout; make the order-service submit path degrade gracefully (skip/queue the exchange-dependent step) rather than 504.
recommended_actions.rationale: Latency_p99 on order-service (~5300ms) matches the 5000ms exchange upstream timeout, and the breaker only opened ~2 minutes into the failure, so users see 504s for the full timeout window.

recommended_actions.action: Engage the external exchange partner and confirm/obtain partner-side status for api.exchange-partner.example for the window starting ~11:01Z, since the failing hop has no in-platform telemetry; escalate per the previous exchange-partner-outage playbook.
recommended_actions.rationale: The only failure signals available are gateway-side connect timeouts, upstream 503s and a breaker opening for exchange-api; exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false so the partner must confirm the outage.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery with the specific series that carried the evidence: exchange-gateway error_rate (was ~43-45%), order-service error_rate (was ~30-32%), order-service latency_p99 (~5300ms back toward ~149ms baseline), and the disappearance of the 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' pattern.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact series/patterns that defined onset and can confirm whether the partner has recovered; success is a return of all four to pre-onset baselines.

recommended_actions.action: Retire mutating rollbacks as the default first response for this signature: add a pre-check that inspects the dominant error pattern (exchange-gateway 504/upstream timeout vs a code-path error) before rolling back a release, so an exchange-partner outage does not trigger an unnecessary rollback.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 (the reporter's 'idempotency keys' suspicion) was rejected precisely because the dominant error names exchange-gateway and the rollback did not change the error rate - a pattern check would have avoided the rollback.

recommended_actions.action: Add health/telemetry for the exchange hop: a synthetic placeOrder/quoteSnapshot probe plus partner error-budget and latency SLOs for api.exchange-partner.example, surfaced in the same view as exchange-gateway, and an alert on upstream connect-timeout rate and breaker state.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failing hop is currently blind (has_telemetry:false) and was only detected indirectly through exchange-gateway, which delayed attribution during this incident.

recommended_actions.action: Add an automated discriminating check to the incident playbook: on order-submit 504s, compare exchange-gateway error_rate against order-service error_rate (subset test) and check order-service CPU/db_pool (local-saturation test) before declaring root cause, codifying the errors from the rejected H2/H3/H4 branches.
recommended_actions.rationale: The three rejected hypotheses were each eliminated by a specific observable margin (subset/super-set error rates, flat local resources, unrelated dependency branch) that can be automated into triage.

data_gaps: No telemetry exists for the failing hop itself: exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false, so the partner-side outage is inferred from gateway-side symptoms (connect timeouts, 503s, breaker) and cannot be directly observed in-platform.
No partner-side status page, error budget, or incident record for api.exchange-partner.example was queried, so the external event behind the 11:01Z onset is unconfirmed.

No independent order-service error_rate query was run specifically for the 11:16-13:00Z post-rollback period; the 'rollback did not fix it' conclusion rests on the existing F8/F10/F11 series rather than an independent pull, so a transient change at exactly 11:16Z could have been missed.

get_deployments returned only a rolled_back_at field for dep-5333 - no rollback deploy record, revert commit/PR id, or rollback event id - so whether the rollback was actually executed and completed is unverified.

exchange-gateway's own cpu_pct/memory_pct/latency_p99 were never queried, so exchange-gateway-internal resource saturation as a contributor to the upstream timeouts cannot be fully excluded (only dismissed on mechanism evidence: the error text names the external host).
inventory-service error_rate query returned budget_exhausted and never executed, so the blast radius is incomplete; other order-service dependents were not checked either.
No database or queue component metrics (order DB, exchange-gateway DB) were inspected around onset, so local saturation at those components is not addressed.

The order-service INFO/WARN log query (including any v2.15.2 deploy/startup line) returned budget_exhausted, so the exact deploy timestamp could not be confirmed directly and onset-vs-deploy correlation remains indirect.

No metric queries were run for ledger-db/kafka/redis-cache saturation in this window; the ruling-out of shared-component contribution comes from the absence of local saturation on order-service, not from direct evidence at those components.

The historical-incident search for pricing-engine/quote-cache-TTL/deployment-regression precedent was never executed (budget exhausted), so there is no precedent evidence on whether a cache.ttl_seconds reduction causes order-submit failures.

Historical incident results provided only id/title/root_cause summaries with no resolution timelines, so precedents remain leads only and cannot be compared quantitatively to the current resolution window.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Partner-side confirmation that the external exchange API was healthy from 11:01Z onward, or partner status showing no incident, would remove the external cause and push the investigation back toward H2/H3/H4.

Discovery that the dep-5333 rollback never actually executed (e.g. the 'rolled_back' status was stale and v2.15.2 still served traffic) would invalidate the key 'rollback did not help' argument and could re-open H2.
An order-service error_rate query showing a sharp return to ~0.2% at exactly 11:16Z would show the rollback did fix the symptom and point to the deployment after all.

Evidence that the dominant errors are code-path errors rather than exchange-gateway 504s (e.g. a local order-submit stack trace, NPE, or duplicate-idempotency-key error dominating at 11:02+) would contradict the external-cause signature.

Exchange-gateway-internal saturation at onset (very high CPU/thread/connection usage inside the gateway itself, with the external peer healthy) would move the cause to H4 (gateway capacity) rather than the external partner.

Evidence that other ledger-db/kafka/redis-cache sharers (portfolio-service, settlement-service, notification-service) degraded at the same time would raise a shared-component cause not currently represented in the ranking.
A retroactive config/flag/network change on exchange-gateway or order-service found in the 11:00-11:01Z window would displace the external-outage explanation.
